constraints: Do not add new claims or on-screen text

whole_dimensions.opening_interest: In the first seconds, which version gives this viewer a clearer reason to keep watching?
whole_dimensions.comprehension: By the end, which version leaves this viewer understanding what happened and why?
whole_dimensions.information_progression: Which version adds new information or meaning at a better rate, without confusing jumps or needless repetition?
whole_dimensions.pacing: Which version's pacing better fits what is shown and said at each moment (neither rushed nor dragging)?
whole_dimensions.visual_narration_alignment: Which version's pictures better show what is being said at the same moment?
whole_dimensions.emotional_effect: Which version creates more curiosity, anticipation, surprise or delight at the right moments?
whole_dimensions.payoff: Which version lands its final point or payoff more clearly?
whole_dimensions.memorability: Which version is this viewer more likely to remember or retell?

region_dimensions.clarity: In this stretch, which version makes what is happening easier to follow?
region_dimensions.curiosity_or_anticipation: In this stretch, which version builds or keeps more curiosity or anticipation?
region_dimensions.visual_narration_alignment: In this stretch, which version's pictures better show what is being said?
region_dimensions.pacing: In this stretch, which version's timing better fits what is shown and said?

whole.words: timed words of the rendered speech

rubric.verdict_rules: Each dimension is asked in both presentation orders (repeats=1). Same label in both orders -> that label; 'same' in both -> same; different answers -> unstable; no valid answer -> unclear. Votes are kept.
rubric.instruction_template:
Frames with timestamps under 100 s belong to Version 1; frames at 100 s or later belong to Version 2 (subtract 100 s).
Both versions present the same idea. They are {scope_text}.
The viewing situation for both: {encounter}. The intended viewer: {audience}. The purpose of the video: {objective}.{payoff}
You did not hear the audio; the words are a transcript of the rendered speech with times.
Answer every question with '1', '2', 'same' (no meaningful difference) or 'unclear' (these frames and words cannot tell), and one short, blunt reason tied to what you saw or read: say plainly what is worse in the losing version, not polite generalities.
Questions:
{questions}
Finally, overall: which version better serves this viewer and purpose {overall_text}?
